source: Holton, Mackridge & Philippaki-Warburton, Greek: An Essential Grammar, 2nd ed. (Routledge, 2016), upload afb4adc8 (PDF pp. 1-34 = §10.9.2-10.25, remainder of Ch 10 'The sentence'). Copyrighted, no open license: rules restated in our own words; examples kept short.

sections.title: Free relative clauses
sections.rule: A free relative clause does not modify a noun; it stands in for a noun phrase. It is introduced by a correlative pronoun/determiner (όποιος, οποιοσδήποτε 'anyone'; ό,τι, οτιδήποτε 'anything'; όσος 'as much as') or by a correlative adverb (όπου 'wherever', όποτε 'whenever', όπως 'however', όσο 'as much as'). Pronoun and determiner uses both occur (e.g. ό,τι on its own, or ό,τι + noun). Prepositional/adverbial phrases can also introduce them. When the relative clause follows the main clause, is the direct object, and όποιος is the subject of the relative clause, όποιος takes the accusative (όποιον). An όσος clause may be answered by a τόσος clause. Any correlative word may be reinforced by κι αν or και να to stress 'no matter'.

examples.el: Εκεί βρίσκεις ό,τι ζητά η ψυχούλα σου.
examples.en: There you find whatever your heart desires.

examples.el: Εκεί βρίσκεις ό,τι φαγητό ζητά η ψυχούλα σου.
examples.en: There you find whatever food your heart desires.

examples.el: Κουτσομπολεύει όποιον συναντήσει.
examples.en: (S)he gossips about anyone (s)he may meet.

examples.el: Στο σπίτι της, όπου/οπουδήποτε κοιτάξεις, θα δεις λουλούδια.
examples.en: In her house, wherever you look you will see flowers.

examples.el: Συμπαθεί μόνο όποιον την κολακεύει.
examples.en: She likes only whoever flatters her.

examples.el: Φοβάται οποιονδήποτε την πλησιάζει.
examples.en: She is afraid of anyone who approaches her.

examples.el: Σου έφερα σύκα να φας όσα θέλεις.
examples.en: I brought you figs so you can eat as many as you want.

examples.el: Όσοι δεν φέρουν την εργασία τους εγκαίρως τους απορρίπτει.
examples.en: (S)he fails those who do not bring their work on time.

examples.el: Όσο κι αν τον βασανίζει, αυτός την αγαπά.
examples.en: No matter how much she torments him, he loves her.

examples.el: Όσα μου ζητήσεις, τόσα θα σου δώσω.
examples.en: I will give you however many you ask for.

examples.el: Με όποιον μιλήσεις, το ίδιο θα σου πει.
examples.en: Whoever you speak to, they'll tell you the same thing.

examples.el: Όπως του μιλήσεις, έτσι θα σου μιλήσει κι αυτός.
examples.en: He will speak to you as you speak to him.

examples.el: Εγώ θα σε περιμένω όποτε κι αν έρθεις.
examples.en: I will wait for you whenever you come.

examples.el: Όπου και να πάω, αυτήν συναντώ.
examples.en: Wherever I go I meet her.

examples.el: Όσο κι αν επιμένεις δεν θα με πείσεις.
examples.en: However much you insist, you will not persuade me.

sections.title: Indirect questions
sections.rule: Indirect questions follow verbs of asking, wondering and equivalent expressions.

sections.title: Questioning the whole sentence
sections.rule: A yes/no indirect question is introduced by αν 'whether' or μήπως 'by any chance', with the verb in the indicative. It can instead be a bare subjunctive with να (no αν/μήπως), because the direct-speech version is a deliberative question ('Should I...?').

examples.el: Δεν με ρώτησαν ποτέ αν με ενοχλεί η μουσική τους (ή όχι).
examples.en: They never asked me whether their music bothers me (or not).

examples.el: Απορώ αν καταλαβαίνει τίποτα.
examples.en: I wonder whether (s)he understands anything.

examples.el: Αναρωτιέται μήπως της λένε ψέματα.
examples.en: She's wondering whether by any chance they're lying to her.

examples.el: Με ρώτησε πολλές φορές να τον παντρευτεί ή όχι.
examples.en: She asked me several times whether she should marry him or not.

sections.title: Questioning one constituent (wh- questions)
sections.rule: A questioned noun phrase is introduced by the question word (see 10.6), alone as a pronoun or as a determiner before a noun. A questioned genitive that belongs to another noun phrase may be placed before or after it (ποιανού/τίνος ο πατέρας, or ο πατέρας ποιανού). Prepositional and adverbial phrases can be questioned too. A question about profession or quality uses τι; about a noun's character use τι είδους + noun or colloquially τι σόι + noun. The verb is indicative, or subjunctive with να.

examples.el: Απορώ ποιος πήγε και του τα είπε.
examples.en: I wonder who went and told him.

examples.el: Δεν ξέρω ποιον υπάλληλο θα απολύσουν.
examples.en: I don't know which employee they will fire.

examples.el: Αναρωτιέται ποιανού πρέπει να δώσει το αυτοκίνητο.
examples.en: (S)he is wondering who (s)he should give the car to.

examples.el: Ρώτησαν ποιανού/τίνος ο πατέρας ήταν γιατρός.
examples.en: They asked whose father was a doctor.

examples.el: Ρώτησαν ο πατέρας ποιανού ήταν γιατρός.
examples.en: They asked whose father was a doctor.

examples.el: Δεν μας εξήγησαν με ποιο δικαίωμα τα κάνουν αυτά.
examples.en: They didn't explain to us by what right they do these things.

examples.el: Ρώτησέ την από ποιο μαγαζί πήρε τα παπούτσια της.
examples.en: Ask her which store she bought her shoes from.

examples.el: Αναρωτιέμαι τι είναι ο κ. Παπαδάκης, καθηγητής ή γιατρός;
examples.en: I wonder what Mr Papadakis is, a teacher or a doctor?

examples.el: Απορώ τι είδους άνθρωπος είναι αυτός τελοσπάντων.
examples.en: I wonder what sort of man he is after all.

examples.el: Πες μου λοιπόν τι σόι αδερφός είναι αυτός.
examples.en: Now tell me what kind of brother he is.

examples.el: Ας μας πει εκείνη ποιον να καλέσουμε.
examples.en: Let her tell us who to invite.

examples.el: Ρώτησέ τον από ποιον δρόμο να πάμε.
examples.en: Ask him which way we should go.

sections.title: Indirect commands
sections.rule: Direct commands normally use the imperative; indirect commands use the subjunctive (να + verb). In direct negative commands (10.4) να is optional, but in indirect negative commands να is obligatory, followed by μη(ν).

examples.el: Του ζήτησε να την αφήσει ήσυχη.
examples.en: She asked him to leave her in peace.

examples.el: Τον παρακαλέσαμε να τη συνοδεύσει στον χορό.
examples.en: We asked him to accompany her to the dance.

examples.el: Τον διέταξε να μη μιλάει.
examples.en: (S)he ordered him not to speak.

examples.el: Απαιτώ να μη με διακόπτεις.
examples.en: I demand that you do not interrupt me.

sections.title: Complement clauses (overview)
sections.rule: Complement clauses can accompany a verb, a noun or an adjective.

examples.el: Μου έλεγε ότι δεν του αρέσουν τα ψάρια.
examples.en: He was telling me that he doesn't like fish.

examples.el: Η Ειρήνη θέλει να σπουδάσει μουσική.
examples.en: Irene wants to study music.

examples.el: Λυπήθηκα πολύ που στενοχωρήθηκε ο Στέφανος.
examples.en: I was very sorry that Stephen got upset.

examples.el: Δεν του αρέσει η ιδέα να παντρευτούν τόσο γρήγορα.
examples.en: He doesn't like the idea of them getting married so soon.

examples.el: Είναι σίγουρος ότι τον αδικούν.
examples.en: He's sure that they're being unfair to him.

sections.title: Complement clauses as objects of a verb
sections.rule: Indicative complements come in three kinds. (a) After verbs of saying, thinking, believing: ότι or πως 'that'. (b) After verbs of psychological state (joy, sorrow, regret): που. (c) After verbs of fear: μήπως; μήπως is not itself negative and is negated with δεν. These complementizers (ότι/πως, που, μήπως) cannot be omitted, unlike English 'that'. Subjunctive complements (να, negated with μην) follow verbs of wishing, hoping, planning, requesting, promising, and also verbs of perception (where English often has -ing). Some verbs of saying/thinking take either ότι or να: the ότι-clause is a more objective judgement, the να-clause is more subjective, coloured with wishing. After verbs of perception, an ότι-clause conveys information rather than direct perception. ξέρω and μαθαίνω with ότι convey knowledge as information, with να convey ability/skill. A neuter weak pronoun on the main verb may anticipate the complement clause (often with ότι, sometimes να or που).

examples.el: Όλοι πιστεύουν ότι/πως ο πόλεμος θα συνεχιστεί.
examples.en: Everybody believes (that) the war will continue.

examples.el: Μου είπε ότι/πως δεν σε ξέρει.
examples.en: (S)he told me (that) (s)he doesn't know you.

examples.el: Μετάνιωσε που τους είπε την αλήθεια.
examples.en: (S)he regretted telling them the truth.

examples.el: Λυπήθηκε που δεν κατάφερε να τον δει.
examples.en: (S)he was sorry (that) (s)he didn't manage to see him.

examples.el: Ανησυχώ μήπως του συνέβη κάτι.
examples.en: I'm worried (that) something may have happened to him.

examples.el: Ανησυχώ μήπως δεν έρθει.
examples.en: I'm worried (that) (s)he may not come.

examples.el: Θα θέλαμε απλώς να της μιλήσουμε.
examples.en: We would just like to speak to her.

examples.el: Θα φροντίσω να έρθω νωρίς.
examples.en: I'll take care to come early.

examples.el: Ελπίζω να μην αργήσει ο Γιάννης.
examples.en: I hope (that) John won't be late.

examples.el: Τον είδαμε να περπατάει πολύ βιαστικός.
examples.en: We saw him walking in a great hurry.

examples.el: Δεν θα ακούσεις την Κλεία να παραπονιέται ποτέ.
examples.en: You'll never hear Clea complaining.

examples.el: Την ένιωσα να τρέμει.
examples.en: I felt her trembling.

examples.el: Πιστεύω ότι θα μας πληρώσουν την άλλη Δευτέρα.
examples.en: I believe (that) they will pay us next Monday.

examples.el: Πιστεύω να μας πληρώσουν την άλλη Δευτέρα.
examples.en: I believe (that) they might pay us next Monday.

examples.el: Ακούσαμε ότι πούλησε και το σπίτι.
examples.en: We heard that (s)he sold the house too.

examples.el: Έμαθε ότι της έλεγαν ψέματα.
examples.en: She found out (that) they were lying to her.

examples.el: Ξέρει ότι είναι πολύ καλός στη δουλειά του.
examples.en: He knows (that) he's very good at his work.

examples.el: Έμαθε να μη δίνει πολλή σημασία στα λόγια του.
examples.en: (S)he learned not to take much notice of his words.

examples.el: Ξέρει να φτιάχνει πολύ νόστιμα ντολμαδάκια.
examples.en: (S)he knows how to make very tasty dolmadakia.

examples.el: Δεν το κατάλαβα ότι ήθελες να μου μιλήσεις.
examples.en: I didn't realize (that) you wanted to speak to me.

examples.el: Το μετάνιωσες ότι/που ήρθες;
examples.en: Have you regretted coming?

examples.el: Το ήθελε πολύ να τον συναντήσει.
examples.en: (S)he wanted very much to meet him.

complementizers: να (μην): wishing, hoping, planning, requesting, perception, ability

sections.title: Complement clauses with impersonal verbs or expressions
sections.rule: Impersonal verbs (φαίνεται, πειράζει, αρέσει) and impersonal expressions (είναι καλό, λυπηρό, σωστό, κρίμα) take a complement clause as subject, introduced by ότι, που or να depending on meaning.

examples.el: Μου φαίνεται ότι θα αργήσουν πάλι.
examples.en: It seems to me (that) they'll be late again.

examples.el: Τον πειράζει που του μιλάει έτσι απότομα.
examples.en: It bothers him that (s)he speaks to him so sharply.

examples.el: Σου αρέσει να ταξιδεύεις;
examples.en: Do you like to travel?

examples.el: Είναι φανερό ότι η κατάσταση θα χειροτερέψει.
examples.en: It's obvious that the situation will get worse.

examples.el: Είναι πιθανόν να φύγουμε την Κυριακή.
examples.en: It's likely (that) we'll be leaving on Sunday.

examples.el: Είναι κρίμα που δεν θα συναντηθούμε τελικά.
examples.en: It's a pity (that) we won't meet after all.

sections.title: Complement clauses governed by adjectives and nouns
sections.rule: A complement clause can depend on an adjective or on a noun, with ότι, που or να according to meaning.

examples.el: Είναι λυπημένος που θα φύγεις.
examples.en: He's sad (that) you're leaving.

examples.el: Είναι συνηθισμένη να την περιποιούνται.
examples.en: She's used to being pampered.

examples.el: Είναι σίγουρη ότι την παρακολουθούν.
examples.en: She's certain (that) they're following her.

examples.el: Ζει με τον φόβο ότι θα της κάνουν διάρρηξη.
examples.en: She lives with the fear that she'll be burgled.

examples.el: Έχει μεγάλη χαρά που θα τον ξαναδεί.
examples.en: (S)he's very happy (that) (s)he's going to see him again.

sections.title: Clauses functioning as noun phrases
sections.rule: A complement clause acting as subject or object of a verb, or object of a preposition, is introduced by the neuter definite article το. When the clause is the object, the main verb may carry the neuter weak pronoun το. The article is generally present when the clause comes at the start of the sentence.

examples.el: Το ότι είναι ξεροκέφαλος είναι γνωστό σε όλους.
examples.en: It is known to everybody that he is stubborn.

examples.el: Το ότι είναι ξεροκέφαλος το ξέρουν όλοι.
examples.en: Everybody knows (that) he is stubborn.

examples.el: Το να προσπαθείς να τον πείσεις είναι μάταιο.
examples.en: It's futile to try to convince him.

examples.el: Δεν θα τον πείσεις με το να γκρινιάζεις συνέχεια.
examples.en: You won't persuade him by grumbling all the time.

examples.el: Με το που τον είδε να μπαίνει, έγινε κατακόκκινη.
examples.en: The moment she saw him coming in, she turned bright red.

sections.title: Conditional constructions
sections.rule: A conditional construction has a protasis (if-clause) and an apodosis (main clause). Typical introducers: αν, εάν, άμα 'if'; έτσι και 'if so much as'; είτε... είτε 'whether... or'; σε περίπτωση που 'in the event that'; εφόσον 'provided that'. More elaborate: εκτός (κι) αν 'unless'; (ακόμη) κι αν 'even if'; έστω κι αν 'even if'. The negative in these protases is δεν. A protasis may occasionally be introduced by subjunctive να (negated by μην). The protasis may precede or follow the apodosis. Conditionals are factual or counterfactual.

conditional_conjunctions: σε περίπτωση που (in the event that)

sections.title: Factual conditional clauses
sections.rule: If the protasis is fulfilled, the apodosis is, has been, will be or can be fulfilled too. In the protasis any tense or aspect may be used except the pluperfect; the apodosis may contain a verb in any form.

examples.el: Αν προσπαθείς να τον πείσεις, κάνεις μεγάλο λάθος.
examples.en: If you're trying to persuade him, you're making a big mistake.

examples.el: Αν (θα) τον παρακαλέσεις θα σου κάνει τη χάρη.
examples.en: If you ask him, he'll do you the favour.

examples.el: Να τον δεις τώρα θα τον λυπηθείς.
examples.en: If you see him now, you'll feel sorry for him.

examples.el: Αν συναντήθηκαν, μάλλον θα μίλησαν και γι' αυτό το θέμα.
examples.en: If they met, they most probably spoke about this matter too.

examples.el: Έτσι και της χαμογελάσει γλυκά, τον συγχωρεί αμέσως.
examples.en: If he so much as smiles at her sweetly, she immediately forgives him.

examples.el: Είτε του μιλάς είτε δεν του μιλάς, το ίδιο κάνει.
examples.en: Whether you speak to him or don't speak to him, it makes no difference.

examples.el: Αν σε πείραξε αυτό που είπα, σου ζητώ συγνώμη.
examples.en: If you got upset by what I said, I ask your forgiveness.

examples.el: Άμα σε ενοχλεί ο καπνός, άνοιξε το παράθυρο.
examples.en: If the smoke bothers you, open the window.

examples.el: Αν τελειώσετε νωρίς ελάτε να μας δείτε.
examples.en: If you finish early come and see us.

sections.title: Counterfactual conditionals
sections.rule: The protasis describes a situation not realised in the past or not realised now, so the apodosis is also unrealised. The protasis verb is imperfect or pluperfect; the apodosis is conditional (θα + imperfect/aorist) or perfect conditional (θα + pluperfect). If the sentence refers to the past, any of these may be used. If it does not refer to the past, only imperfect and conditional may be used, so an imperfect + conditional sentence can mean past, present or future.

examples.el: Αν έστελνε εκείνο το γράμμα θα τον είχε πείσει.
examples.en: If (s)he had sent that letter (s)he would have persuaded him.

examples.el: Αν είχε στείλει εκείνο το γράμμα θα τον έπειθε.
examples.en: If (s)he had sent that letter (s)he would have persuaded him.

examples.el: Αν είχε στείλει εκείνο το γράμμα θα τον είχε πείσει.
examples.en: If (s)he had sent that letter (s)he would have persuaded him.

examples.el: Αν έστελνε εκείνο το γράμμα θα τον έπειθε.
examples.en: If (s)he sent that letter (s)he would persuade him / if (s)he had sent it (s)he would have persuaded him.

examples.el: Αν καταλάβαινες τη στενοχώρια μου δεν θα μιλούσες έτσι.
examples.en: If you understood my distress you wouldn't speak like this / if you had understood you wouldn't have spoken like that.

examples.el: Δεν θα τον παντρευόταν ποτέ αν δεν τον αγαπούσε.
examples.en: She would never marry him if she didn't love him / would never have married him if she hadn't loved him.

sections.title: Concessive clauses
sections.rule: Indicative concessive clauses are introduced by αν και 'although', ακόμη κι αν 'even if/though', παρά το ότι, παρ' όλο που, παρ' όλον ότι, μολονότι, μ' όλο που, παρά το γεγονός ότι 'in spite of the fact that'. They usually precede the main clause but may follow it. Subjunctive concessives are introduced by κι ας 'even if/though' and negated with μην.

examples.el: Αν και δεν διαβάζει πολύ, ξέρει πολλά πράγματα.
examples.en: Although (s)he doesn't read much, (s)he knows a lot.

examples.el: Παρ' όλο που τον προειδοποιήσαμε, δεν μας άκουσε.
examples.en: Although we warned him, he didn't listen to us.

examples.el: Παρά το ότι έχει πολλά λεφτά, τσιγκουνεύεται πολύ.
examples.en: In spite of the fact that (s)he has a lot of money, (s)he's tight-fisted.

examples.el: Μου αρέσει πολύ αυτό το σπίτι, κι ας είναι μικρό.
examples.en: I like this house very much, even though it's small.

examples.el: Εκείνη αποφάσισε να πάει, κι ας μην είχε πρόσκληση.
examples.en: She decided to go even though she didn't have an invitation.

sections.title: Temporal clauses
sections.rule: Temporal clauses say whether the subordinate action is before, after or simultaneous with the main one. Most common conjunction: όταν 'when'. Others: σαν, όποτε, οπόταν 'whenever', οπότε 'at which point', τώρα που 'now that', τότε που 'at the time that', αφού, μετά που 'after', αφότου, από τότε που 'since', ώσπου 'until', ενώ, όσο, ενόσω, την ώρα που 'while', καθώς 'as', μόλις 'as soon as', εφόσον 'as long as', πάνω που 'just as'. Όταν, μόλις, αφού, όποτε may be followed by the subjunctive (dependent) when not referring to the past. Ενώ, όσο, ενόσω, την ώρα που are typically followed by present or imperfect. Πριν and προτού 'before' combine only with the dependent (subjunctive), with or without να. Μέχρι 'until' takes που + indicative for a real action; ώσπου and μέχρι take να for a potential rather than real action.

examples.el: Όταν λείπει η γάτα χορεύουν τα ποντίκια!
examples.en: When the cat's away the mice will play!

examples.el: Όταν διάβασε το μήνυμά του συγκινήθηκε πολύ.
examples.en: When (s)he read his message (s)he was very moved.

examples.el: Αφού τελειώσεις, πάρε με τηλέφωνο.
examples.en: After you finish, call me.

examples.el: Όποτε το αποφασίσεις έλα.
examples.en: Come whenever you decide.

examples.el: Μόλις τον δει θα καταλάβει ότι είναι θυμωμένος.
examples.en: As soon as (s)he sees him (s)he'll realize he's angry.

examples.el: Την ώρα που έπινε τον καφέ του, του εξήγησα το πρόβλημα.
examples.en: While he was drinking his coffee, I explained the problem to him.

examples.el: Πρέπει να μιλήσεις με τον Νίκο πριν (να) πουλήσεις το σπίτι.
examples.en: You must speak to Nick before you sell the house.

examples.el: Έτρωγε μέχρι που έσκασε.
examples.en: (S)he kept on eating until (s)he burst.

examples.el: Θα επιμένω μέχρι να σε πείσω.
examples.en: I will persist until I persuade you.

sections.title: Clauses of manner
sections.rule: Manner clauses are introduced by όπως and καθώς 'as', or by έτσι που 'in such a way' and όπως κι αν 'in whatever way'. The verb is indicative.

examples.el: Τα πράγματα είναι δυστυχώς όπως μου τα περιέγραψες.
examples.en: Matters are unfortunately as you described them to me.

examples.el: Μαγείρεψε τις αγγινάρες έτσι που της είχε δείξει η γιαγιά της.
examples.en: She cooked the artichokes as her grandmother had shown her.

examples.el: Όπως κι αν το δούμε το πράγμα, η Ειρήνη έχει δίκιο.
examples.en: No matter how we look at it, Irene is right.

sections.title: Clauses of purpose (final clauses)
sections.rule: Purpose clauses are typically introduced by για followed immediately by να; nothing may come between them. After verbs of motion για may be dropped.

examples.el: Την καλέσαμε και εκείνη για να μην παραπονιέται.
examples.en: We invited her too in order to prevent her complaining.

examples.el: Ήρθε (για) να την δει αλλά εκείνη έλειπε.
examples.en: (S)he came to see her but she was out.

sections.title: Clauses of result
sections.rule: Result clauses are introduced by που or ώστε 'so that', followed by an indicative or subjunctive verb. The main clause often has τόσος 'so much', τέτοιος 'such', έτσι (formal ούτως) or με τέτοιο τρόπο 'in such a way'. Unlike English 'that', που/ώστε cannot be omitted. Result can also be expressed by για να.

examples.el: Δεν πρέπει να της λέμε τίποτα ώστε να αποφασίσει μόνη της.
examples.en: We mustn't say anything to her so that she can decide on her own.

examples.el: Δεν βρίσκει παπούτσια που να της κάνουνε.
examples.en: She can't find shoes that will fit her.

examples.el: Έχει πει τόσα ψέματα που κανείς δεν τον πιστεύει πια.
examples.en: He has told so many lies (that) nobody believes him any more.

examples.el: Έχτισαν το σπίτι έτσι (ή με τέτοιο τρόπο) που να αντέχει στους σεισμούς.
examples.en: They built the house in such a way that it will withstand earthquakes.

examples.el: Θα σου εξηγήσουμε την κατάσταση έτσι (ή ούτως) ώστε να έχεις μια πλήρη εικόνα.
examples.en: We'll explain the situation to you in such a way that you will have a complete picture.

examples.el: Πρέπει να είσαι πολύ τυχερός για να βρεις τέτοιο φίλο.
examples.en: You have to be very lucky to find such a friend.

sections.title: Clauses of cause
sections.rule: Cause clauses use γιατί or more formal διότι 'because', καθώς 'as', επειδή 'because', αφού, εφόσον, μια και 'since', with an indicative verb. Γιατί/διότι clauses generally follow the main clause; the others can precede or follow it.

examples.el: Δεν θα σας πληρώσουμε, γιατί/διότι δεν έχουμε λεφτά.
examples.en: We won't pay you, because we don't have any money.

examples.el: Επειδή δεν κοιμήθηκε χθες το βράδυ, νιώθει πολύ κουρασμένος.
examples.en: Because he didn't sleep last night, he feels very tired.

examples.el: Αφού σου ορκίστηκε, πρέπει να τον πιστέψεις.
examples.en: Since he gave you his word, you have to believe him.

examples.el: Κάνε λοιπόν ό,τι θέλεις, αφού επιμένεις τόσο πολύ.
examples.en: Do what you like then, since you insist so much.

examples.el: Μια και είσαι τώρα εδώ, έλα να με βοηθήσεις.
examples.en: As you're here now, come and help me.

sections.title: Word order
sections.rule: Because Greek marks subject (nominative) and direct object (accusative) by form, word order is much freer than in English; all five orders of subject, verb and object below mean roughly the same thing (neutral orders are SVO and VSO).

examples.el: Ο σκύλος δάγκωσε τον Μιχάλη.
examples.en: The dog bit Michael.

examples.el: Τον Μιχάλη δάγκωσε ο σκύλος.
examples.en: The dog bit Michael.

examples.el: Τον Μιχάλη ο σκύλος τον δάγκωσε.
examples.en: The dog bit Michael.

examples.el: Δάγκωσε ο σκύλος τον Μιχάλη.
examples.en: The dog bit Michael.

examples.el: Δάγκωσε τον Μιχάλη ο σκύλος.
examples.en: The dog bit Michael.

sections.title: Topicalization and focusing
sections.rule: Focus is the new, emphasised information; topic is what is already known. Greek, like English, marks focus with heavy stress, but its main device is the presence or absence of a doubling weak pronoun for the object. SVO/VSO without a pronoun = all new information (no topic, no focus). Object plus doubling pronoun = the object is the topic, and the focus is another element (subject, verb or adverbial, whichever is stressed). Object fronted without a doubling pronoun = the object is the focus. Indirect objects behave identically. To emphasise a non-object element, add the doubling pronoun; the object may optionally precede the verb.

examples.el: Τον Μιχάλη τον δάγκωσε ο σκύλος.
examples.en: It was the dog that bit Michael (Michael = topic).

examples.el: Του Γιάννη δεν θα δώσουνε αύξηση.
examples.en: It's John they won't give a pay rise to (focus on John).

examples.el: Του Γιάννη δεν θα του δώσουνε αύξηση.
examples.en: They won't give a pay rise to John (John = topic).

examples.el: Τον Μιχάλη τον δάγκωσε χθες ο σκύλος.
examples.en: The dog bit Michael yesterday (focus: yesterday).

examples.el: Ο σκύλος τον δάγκωσε χθες τον Μιχάλη.
examples.en: It was yesterday the dog bit Michael.

sections.title: Co-ordination
sections.rule: Clauses, phrases or single words can be co-ordinated. Common conjunctions: και 'and' (κι before a vowel), ή 'or', είτε... είτε 'either... or / whether... or', αλλά or colloquial μα 'but', ούτε... ούτε 'neither... nor', όμως 'however'. Όμως links clauses only and can stand between the clauses, at the end of the second, or inside the second. Και, ούτε, είτε and ή may stand before both items, with heavy stress. Και may also replace a subordinating conjunction: να/που after verbs of perception; να after verbs of beginning/continuing (αρχίζω, συνεχίζω, εξακολουθώ); result (ώστε να); a relative clause (που); reason (γιατί); condition (and = 'if you do... then').

sections.title: Co-ordination of clauses
sections.rule: Examples of clause co-ordination.

examples.el: Αύριο θα δω τον Γιάννη και θα του μιλήσω για σένα.
examples.en: Tomorrow I'll see John and I'll speak to him about you.

examples.el: Θα τηλεφωνήσω στον Νίκο αλλά δεν θα τον καλέσω εδώ.
examples.en: I'll phone Nick but I won't invite him here.

examples.el: Τελικά θα μου πεις τι συμβαίνει ή να ρωτήσω την Ελένη;
examples.en: Finally will you tell me what's going on, or should I ask Helen?

examples.el: Εγώ πάντως θα πάω, είτε έρθεις είτε δεν έρθεις.
examples.en: In any case I will go, whether you come or not.

examples.el: Ούτε έφαγα ούτε ήπια τίποτα από χθες.
examples.en: I have neither eaten nor drunk anything since yesterday.

examples.el: Της το είπα μα δεν θέλει να το πιστέψει.
examples.en: I told her but she doesn't want to believe it.

examples.el: Θα σε περιμένω στο γραφείο, όμως μην καθυστερήσεις.
examples.en: I'll be waiting for you at the office but don't be late.

examples.el: Θα φάμε μαζί, τον λογαριασμό όμως θα τον πληρώσω εγώ.
examples.en: We'll eat together but I'll pay the bill.

sections.title: Co-ordination of other constituents
sections.rule: Phrases and words may be co-ordinated with the same conjunctions; και can replace other conjunctions as listed under 10.21.

examples.el: Θα αγοράσω το κίτρινο πουκάμισο και τη μαύρη τσάντα.
examples.en: I will buy the yellow shirt and the black bag.

examples.el: Πρέπει να διαλέξεις τον Σπύρο ή εμένα.
examples.en: You have to choose Spiros or me.

examples.el: Δεν της μίλησε η Μαρία αλλά η Ελένη.
examples.en: It wasn't Mary but Helen who spoke to her.

examples.el: Μου αρέσει με ή (και) χωρίς λάδι.
examples.en: I like it with or without oil.

examples.el: Θέλουν και την πίτα ολόκληρη και τον σκύλο χορτάτο.
examples.en: They want both the dog well fed and the pie whole.

examples.el: Δεν είναι ούτε ψηλός ούτε κοντός.
examples.en: He's neither tall nor short.

examples.el: Δεν ξέρω τι να κάνω. Ή θα το πουλήσω ή θα το χαρίσω.
examples.en: I don't know what to do. Either I'll sell it or I'll give it away.

examples.el: Τους άκουσα και ψιθύριζαν.
examples.en: I heard them whispering (και replacing να/που).

examples.el: Άρχισαν και τον παρακολουθούσαν.
examples.en: They started following him.

examples.el: Συνέχιζε και μας έλεγε ψέματα.
examples.en: He continued to lie to us.

examples.el: Τι κάνει και είναι τόσο αντιπαθητικός;
examples.en: What does he do to be so unlikeable?

examples.el: Μπήκε μέσα ένας νεαρός και φορούσε ωραίο κοστούμι.
examples.en: In came a young man (who was) wearing a beautiful suit.

examples.el: Κλείσε την τηλεόραση και θέλω να κοιμηθώ.
examples.en: Switch off the TV because I want to sleep.

examples.el: Κάνε μου αυτή τη χάρη και θα σου δώσω ό,τι θέλεις.
examples.en: Do this favour for me and I will give you whatever you want.

sections.title: Comparison
sections.rule: Comparison uses the comparative of an adjective or adverb (see 3.44 and 7.6). The second member is introduced by από + accusative, or by the genitive of a weak pronoun. Παρά may also introduce it; the second member is then in the same case as the first, and παρά is also used when the compared items are clauses, prepositional phrases or adverbials. The second member may be omitted if clear.

examples.el: Αυτή την εποχή ο σολομός είναι ακριβότερος από τον μπακαλιάρο.
examples.en: At this time of the year salmon is more expensive than cod.

examples.el: Η Ελένη είναι κατά πολύ μεγαλύτερή του.
examples.en: Helen is far older than him.

examples.el: Είναι καλύτερα να μας συνοδεύει ο Νίκος παρά ο Μιχάλης.
examples.en: It's better that Nikos accompanies us rather than Michael.

examples.el: Προτιμώ να του κάνω το χατίρι παρά να τον ακούω να κλαίει.
examples.en: I prefer to do what he wants than to hear him cry.

examples.el: Δουλεύω πιο καλά στο γραφείο παρά στο σπίτι.
examples.en: I work better in the office than at home.

examples.el: Καλύτερα να έρθεις σήμερα παρά αύριο.
examples.en: It's better that you come today than tomorrow.

examples.el: Νομίζω ότι έτσι είναι καλύτερα.
examples.en: I think that it's better this way.

sections.title: Correlative comparison
sections.rule: Correlative comparison ('the more... the more') shows two elements possessing a quality to the same degree. The first part is introduced by όσο 'as much as', the second by τόσο 'so much', or by the correlative pronoun/determiner όσος and the quantitative τόσος.

examples.el: Όσα άστρα έχει ο ουρανός, τόσες ευχές σου δίνω.
examples.en: I give you as many wishes as the sky has stars.

examples.el: Όσο πιο γελαστός είναι, τόσο περισσότερο νευριάζει η Καίτη.
examples.en: The more cheerful he is the more Kate gets irritated.

examples.el: Όσο πιο πολλά κερδίζει, τόσο πιο τσιγκούνης γίνεται.
examples.en: The more he earns the stingier he becomes.

sections.title: Equation
sections.rule: Equation (A is as X as B): the second member is introduced by σαν, όπως, ως or όσο. Σαν takes the accusative when the second member is a definite noun phrase, the nominative when it is indefinite. Σαν before a να-clause means 'as if'. Ως means 'in the capacity of' rather than 'like'. Όπως introduces a nominative second member. Equation can also be expressed with τόσο before the first member and όσο before the second; the first element may be omitted.

examples.el: Το πεπόνι αυτό είναι γλυκό σαν το μέλι.
examples.en: This melon is sweet like honey.

examples.el: Ο Νίκος είναι έξυπνος σαν τον πατέρα του.
examples.en: Nick's clever like his father.

examples.el: Γελάει σαν χαζός.
examples.en: He's laughing like an idiot.

examples.el: Με κοιτάζει σαν να μη με έχει ξαναδεί.
examples.en: (S)he's looking at me as if (s)he hasn't seen me before.

examples.el: Σου μιλάω ως ειδικός στο θέμα αυτό.
examples.en: I'm speaking to you as a specialist in this subject.

examples.el: Ο Παύλος είναι τεμπέλης όπως (κι) εσύ.
examples.en: Paul is lazy like you.

examples.el: Περπατάει αργά όπως η χελώνα.
examples.en: (S)he walks slowly like a tortoise.

examples.el: Με συγκινεί τόσο η κλασική μουσική όσο και η μοντέρνα.
examples.en: Classical music moves me as much as modern.

examples.el: Είναι άραγε τόσο αδιάφορος όσο θέλει να δείχνει;
examples.en: Is he as indifferent as he wants to appear, I wonder?

examples.el: Δεν είναι σοβαρή όσο εσύ.
examples.en: She's not as serious as you.

sections.title: Reflexive expressions
sections.rule: Three ways to express that the subject is also the patient. (a) The reflexive phrase ο εαυτός μου 'myself' (article + εαυτός + possessive), most often accusative as direct object, also after prepositions; article and noun stay singular even if the possessive is plural. (b) A passive verb form, for some grooming or bodily-care verbs, especially with a human subject. (c) The prefix αυτο- attached to a passive verb, for a few reflexives.

examples.el: Πρέπει να φροντίζεις τον εαυτό σου.
examples.en: You must look after yourself.

examples.el: Μόνο τον εαυτό τους κοιτάζουν και κανέναν άλλο.
examples.en: They only look after themselves and no one else.

examples.el: Πρέπει να έχεις εμπιστοσύνη μόνο στον εαυτό σου.
examples.en: You should only trust yourself.

examples.el: Η Μαρία έχει μεγάλη ιδέα για τον εαυτό της.
examples.en: Mary has a very high opinion of herself.

examples.el: Πρέπει να ντύνεσαι ζεστά τον χειμώνα εδώ.
examples.en: You must dress warmly in the winter here.

examples.el: Θα λουστώ και θα 'ρθω.
examples.en: I'll wash my hair and I'll come.

examples.el: Πάλι χτενίζεσαι;
examples.en: Are you combing your hair again?

examples.el: Ο άνθρωπος αυτός αυτοκαταστράφηκε.
examples.en: This man destroyed himself.

sections.title: Reciprocal expressions
sections.rule: Reciprocals ('one another') are formed in three ways. (a) The periphrasis ο ένας τον άλλο, or μεταξύ + genitive weak pronoun. The first part is nominative; the second takes the gender and case its role requires (accusative object, or a prepositional phrase). When the two parts are separated, the verb is singular. (b) Some verbs of feeling or feeling-motivated actions use the plural passive form reciprocally. (c) The prefix αλληλο- attached to the plural passive of a few verbs.

examples.el: Οι δυο αυτοί φίλοι αγαπούν πολύ ο ένας τον άλλο.
examples.en: These two friends love each other very much.

examples.el: Εμείς οι γυναίκες πρέπει να βοηθούμε η μία την άλλη.
examples.en: We women must help each other.

examples.el: Συναγωνίζονται ο ένας με τον άλλο (ή μεταξύ τους).
examples.en: They compete with each other.

examples.el: Συχνά δίνουν λεφτά ο ένας στον άλλο.
examples.en: They often give money to each other.

examples.el: Το πρόβλημα είναι ότι ο ένας αντιπαθεί τον άλλο.
examples.en: The problem is that the one dislikes the other.

examples.el: Δεν έχει ο ένας εμπιστοσύνη στον άλλο.
examples.en: They do not trust one another.

examples.el: Ο Νίκος και η Όλγα αγαπιούνται πολύ.
examples.en: Nick and Olga love each other very much.

examples.el: Δεν τους είδα ποτέ να φιλιούνται.
examples.en: I've never seen them kiss (each other).

examples.el: Οι καλοί φίλοι αλληλοϋποστηρίζονται.
examples.en: Good friends support one another.

sections.title: Impersonal uses of verbs
sections.rule: Greek impersonal verbs have no subject and appear in the third person singular. Besides always-impersonal verbs (6.6), many verbs can be used impersonally: weather verbs (βρέχει, χιονίζει); impersonal έχει 'there is/are'; φαίνεται 'it seems' (with ότι- or να-clause) and πρόκειται 'be going to' (with να); αρέσει 'it pleases' with a genitive pronoun for 'I like'; the modals πρέπει 'must' and μπορεί 'maybe'.

examples.el: Από τον Οκτώβριο βρέχει σχεδόν κάθε μέρα.
examples.en: Since October it's been raining almost every day.

examples.el: Έχει πολλούς ανθρώπους εκεί μέσα.
examples.en: There are a lot of people in there.

examples.el: Φαίνεται ότι δεν την πιστεύουν.
examples.en: It seems that they don't believe her.

examples.el: Φαίνεται να μην είναι ευχαριστημένος.
examples.en: He doesn't seem to be pleased.

examples.el: Δεν πρόκειται να τον ξεχάσει.
examples.en: (S)he's not about to forget him.

examples.el: Μου αρέσει να σε ακούω να μιλάς.
examples.en: I like to hear you talk.

examples.el: Του αρέσει να ακούει μουσική.
examples.en: He likes listening to music.

examples.el: Πρέπει να τους καλέσουμε.
examples.en: We must invite them.

examples.el: Μπορεί να μην ήταν αυτός ο φταίχτης.
examples.en: Maybe he wasn't the culprit.
